# Targeted discovery interview

Use during interactive analysis or development when an unresolved requirement or decision changes the requested outcome, scope, behavior, rollout, risk or acceptance. Read the supplied request, code, task memory and relevant references first; distinguish source facts, confirmed requirements and open choices.

Ask one question at a time. State the unresolved decision, recommend an option with its reason, and describe the significant consequence or trade-off of the alternative. Do not force a recommendation when evidence is insufficient; explain what is missing.

Before finalizing Planning, establish the outcome, intended users or notification recipients, in-scope domains/environments, expected behavior and observable acceptance criteria where applicable. Use the [initial planning decisions](../workflows/development.md#initial-planning-decisions-and-system-impact) to identify material gaps, including deployment order and service continuity. Ask about choices the available evidence cannot settle; do not invent a threshold, destination, replay policy or environment to make the plan complete.

Reuse answers and approvals already provided. If the requirements are sufficient, proceed without an interview. Resolve routine technical details within the agreed scope and explain consequential choices; do not turn every missing detail into a question or demand exhaustive certainty.

Record approved material decisions in the existing task record. An unanswered question is not approval. Continue independent safe work when possible; pause only the part dependent on the decision.

For automated review, do not run this interview. Report the missing evidence and its impact on review confidence without presenting an assumption as a confirmed defect.
